name: radio-serial-organ-stings
style: 1930s wireless crime serial episode, sound play not a song, no beat, no tune. Cinema theatre organ fires one held stab chord at each scene change, tibia and vox humana stops with heavy tremulant, studio organist cueing danger. Live studio foley in the gaps: paper envelopes riffled, brass counter bell struck once, wooden crate dropped hard on boards, curtain rings rasping along a rail. Older English gentleman announcer, clipped plummy received pronunciation, dry and certain, unhurried, close to the ribbon microphone, speaking plainly. A final low pedal chord swells and sustains under the last words. Narrow mono AM band, valve hiss, shellac surface crackle.
exclude: singing, melody, sung vocals, ragtime, rap, piano, drums, beat, chorus, jazz band, swing, orchestra, synth
lyrics:
[Intro: organ sting]
[envelopes shuffled]
[counter bell]

[organ sting]
[crate thuds down]

[organ sting]
[curtain swish]

[Spoken word]
[Man]
They're going to print the money and the weapon sales will still happen anyway, everything else is a distraction.

[low organ chord holds]
[End]

name: back-room-whisper-upright
style: A short scene, not a song. The back room of a London pub in 1934, thick with pipe smoke. Through the wall, an out-of-tune upright piano picks out a slow, creeping minor-key shuffle, muffled and far off. Close by: glasses clink, men murmur low, a thumb riffles a wad of banknotes, a coin spins on a wooden counter and rattles flat. A young London man leans right into the microphone and whispers, hushed and conspiratorial, like a bookie's runner telling you the fix behind his hand: dry, certain, faintly amused. The room falls silent for his last words. Voice-forward, intimate, real room sound, no melody in the voice.
exclude: singing, sung vocals, choir, chorus hook, drums, beat, bass drop, orchestra, string swell, cinematic score, ragtime, Scott Joplin, synth
lyrics:
[Intro: room ambience, distant muffled upright piano behind a wall, glasses clink, banknotes riffled, a coin spun on the counter]

[Whispered spoken word]
(They're going to print the money and the weapon sales will still happen anyway,

[The room falls silent]
everything else is a distraction.)

[End]

name: novelty-flurry-then-violin-jab
style: 15-second timed cue, solo piano then strings, spoken word, voice-forward. 0-7s: invented 1920s novelty piano showpiece, glittering chromatic right-hand runs, triplet figures, glissando sweeps, cheeky vaudeville bounce, dry woodblock ticking the pulse. 7-10s: the piano stumbles, fumbles a bar, then doubles its speed in a nervous scramble; a brass cash register bell rings once. 10.5s: dead stop, a single sharp violin stab, then a low sustained cello drone alone. Over the drone a very deep, slow, gravelly old man speaks, grandfatherly, unimpressed, weary authority, close dry mic, plain conversational pacing, no melody. Dry 78rpm room tone, intimate, low dynamics after the stab.
exclude: ragtime, Joplin rag, stride piano, The Entertainer, film score pastiche, orchestral swell, sung vocals, singing, choir, chorus, rap, drums, bass guitar, synth
lyrics:
[Intro: 0-7s, solo novelty piano flurry, runs and glissandi, woodblock tick]

[Break: 7-10s, piano trips and doubles up, cash register bell]

[Violin stab, then low cello drone]

[End: cello drone, silence]
